translations.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, an appointed apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
which he promised beforehand through his prophets, from the holy scriptures,
concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
who was shown to be the Son of God by power and by the Spirit of holiness, through the resurrection from the dead of Jesus Christ our Lord,
from whom we have received grace and apostleship, to bring all the Gentiles into obedience to the faith for the sake of his name,
among whom you too are called, you of Christ Jesus,
to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ!
First, I thank my God through Christ Jesus for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, is my witness how unceasingly I make remembrance of you.
In my prayers I always pray for you, that I too may be granted, by the will of God, a successful journey to you,
for I long to see you, so that I too may impart to you some spiritual grace for your strengthening.
And this is the mutual encouragement among you, through the faith we share with one another, yours and mine.
I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I have wanted to come to you and have been hindered until now, so that I might find some fruit among you too, as among the other nations.
I am a debtor to Gentiles and to barbarians, to the wise and to the foolish.
Such is my eagerness to bring the good news to you also who are in Rome.
For I am not ashamed of this gospel, for it is the power of God for the salvation of everyone who believes it, the Jews first and then the Gentiles.
For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, as it is written: The righteous shall live by faith.
For the wrath of God is to be revealed from heaven against all ungodly and false people, who held the truth of God in falsehood,
for the knowledge of God is evident among them, because God himself revealed it to them.

For his invisible nature, his eternal power and divinity, has been clearly seen since the creation of the world, perceived in the things that have been made, so that they are without any answer to give,
for they knew God and did not glorify him as God or give him thanks, but became futile in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
They called themselves wise and became fools
and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of the image of corruptible man and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
Therefore God gave them over to the lust of their hearts for impurity, so that their bodies were dishonored among themselves.
They exchanged the truth of God for falsehood and became irreverent, and they served created things and not the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
Therefore God gave them over to the passion of dishonor, for their women exchanged the natural order for what is against nature.

Likewise their men also abandoned the natural order with women and burned with lust for one another. Men did what is shameful with men, and they receive among themselves the due penalty for their error.
And since they did not see fit to test God so as to hold him in knowledge, God gave them over to that untested mind, to do what is improper;
they were full of all falsehood, wickedness, evil, greed; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits,
whispering, slander; they were afflicters of God, revilers, arrogant, insolent, inventors of evil, disobedient to fathers and mothers,
without understanding, disorderly, unloving, implacable, merciless,
who knew the judgment of God, that those who do such things are worthy of death; and not only did they do this, but they were also pleased with those who did the same.

Therefore you have no answer to give, O man, every one of you who judges; for by the judgment with which you judge your companion, you condemn yourself, because you do the very same thing that you judge.
We know this, that the judgment of God is true concerning those who do such things.
Do you really suppose this, O man, you who judge those who do such things and do the same yourself: that you will somehow escape the judgment of God?
Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and long-suffering? Do you not know that the long-suffering of God leads you to repentance?
But by that hardness of yours and your unrepentant heart you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteousness of the judgment of God,
who will repay each person according to their deeds:
to those who do good work, who seek eternal life: glory, honor and incorruption;
but to those who are of strife, and disobedient to the truth, and obedient to falsehood: wrath and anger.
Affliction and distress upon every human soul that does evil, the Jew first and then the Gentile!
But glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, the Jew first and then the Gentile!
For there is no partiality with God.
For those who sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and those who sinned within the law will also be judged by the law.
For it is not the hearers of the law who will be justified before God, but the doers of the law who will be justified.
For the Gentiles, who do not have the law, also do what belongs to the law by nature; these, because they do not have the law, are themselves a law to themselves:
they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their mind bearing witness with them, and among one another the thoughts of their hearts accusing or else defending them
on that day when God will judge what is hidden in people, according to my gospel, through Christ Jesus.
If you bear the name of Jew, and rest upon the law, and boast in God,
and know his will, and approve what is better, and are instructed by the law,
and trust yourself to be a guide of the blind and a light to those who are in darkness,
a teacher of infants, and you have the form of knowledge and truth in the law,
You who teach your companion, do you not teach yourself?
You who preach against stealing, do you steal? You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you plunder temples?
You who boast in the law, through that transgression of the law of yours you dishonor God.
For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, as it is written.
Now circumcision is of benefit if you keep the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, that circumcision of yours has become uncircumcision for you.
If, then, the uncircumcised man keeps the righteousness of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?
And the one who is by nature [un]circumcised [?], who fulfills the law, will judge you, who with the letter and circumcision have transgressed the law!
For it is not the one who is outwardly a Jew, nor the one who is outwardly circumcised in the flesh,
but the one who is a Jew in secret and has the circumcision of the heart, by the spirit and not by the letter, whose praise is not from men but from God.
What then is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
Much in every way: first of all this, that they were entrusted with the words of God.
What then? If someone has become unfaithful, will his unfaithfulness perhaps nullify the faithfulness of God?
Let it not be! Let God alone be true and every man a liar, as it is written: That you may be justified in your word and prevail in your judgment.
If our falsehood bears out the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is there perhaps falsehood with God, who sends wrath? Am I saying something in a human way?
Let it not be! Otherwise, how would God judge the world?
If the righteousness of God has abounded through that falsehood of mine, to his glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
And is it not as we are slandered, and as some claim that we say: Let us do evil, so that good may come to us? Their judgment lies in condemnation.
What then? Do we excel? Not at all, for we have already charged Jews and Gentiles, all of them, with being under sin.
As it is written: There is no one righteous, not even one;
there is no one who understands, there is no one who seeks out God;
all have turned aside together and become useless; there is no one who would do kindness, there is not even one;
their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they practiced deceit; the venom of asps is on their lips;
their feet are swift to shed blood;
destruction and misery are in their ways;
and the way of peace they have not known.
There is no fear of God before their eyes.
But we know this: that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may be liable to the judgment of God,
for by works of the law no flesh will be justified before him, for from the law comes the recognition of sin.
But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, attested by the law and the prophets,
through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and upon all who believe, for there is no distinction;
all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
and they are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Jesus Christ,
whom God prepared beforehand as a propitiation, through faith, by his own blood, to reveal his righteousness through the forgiveness of former sins,
by the forbearance of God, to reveal his righteousness at this present time, so that he may be righteous and the justifier of the one who is of the faith of Jesus.
Where then is that boasting? It is shut out. By what law? Of works? No, but by the law of faith.
For we hold that a person is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
Or is God the God of the Jews only, and not of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also.
If indeed God is one, who justifies the circumcised from faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith,
do we now nullify the law through faith? Let it not be! Rather, we uphold the law.
What then shall we say? Did Abraham, our father, find anything according to the flesh?
If Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast of, but not before God.
For what does the Scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
Now to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned as grace but as a debt.
But to the one who does not work, and believes in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness.
Just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God reckoned righteousness apart from works:
Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven and whose sins have been covered;
blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not reckoned sin.
Now then, is this blessedness upon circumcision or upon uncircumcision? For we say that Abraham's faith was reckoned to him as righteousness.
When then was it reckoned? Was he still in circumcision or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

And he received circumcision as a sign, as a seal of the righteousness of the faith that he had in uncircumcision, so that he might be the father of all uncircumcised believers, so that it might be reckoned to them as righteousness,
and the father of the circumcised, not only of those who are of the circumcision, but also of those who stand in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants, that he would inherit the world, did not come from the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
If those who are of the law are the heirs, faith is empty and the promises are made void.
For the law brings about wrath, but where there is no law, there is no transgression of the law either.

Therefore it is by faith and by these graces, so that the promise may be firm for all the descendants, not only for those who are of the law, but also for those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,
as it is written: "I have appointed you father of many nations," before God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and orders what does not exist as though it existed.
Against hope, he believed in hope, so that he might become the father of many nations, according to what was said: "So shall your descendants be."
And he did not grow weak in faith, nor did he consider his own self — for his body was dead, as he was about a hundred years old — or the weakness of Sarah's womb.
For he did not waver in unbelief concerning the promise of God, but grew strong in faith and gave glory to God,
and he came to know that he who had promised is also able to do it.
Therefore also it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
It was not written for his sake alone that it was reckoned to him as righteousness,
but also for our sake, to whom it is to be reckoned, we who believe in him who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead,
who was handed over for our sins and rose for our justification.
Now therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
through whom we have also gained access by faith to this grace in which we stand, and we boast in the hope of the glory of God.
And not only this, but we also boast in affliction, knowing that affliction brings about endurance,
and endurance brings about proven character, and proven character brings about hope.
And hope does not put to shame, for the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
For Christ, while we were still weak, at the appointed time died for the ungodly.
For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous person, though for a good person, who knows, someone might dare to face death.
But God showed his own love toward us, for while we were still ungodly, Christ died for us.
How much more now, having been justified by his blood, shall we be saved from wrath through him.
For if while we were still enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, how much more now, having been reconciled, shall we be saved by his saving power!
And not only this, but we also boast in God through Christ Jesus, through whom we have now received this reconciliation.
Therefore, just as through that one man sin entered the world, and through sin, death, and so death came upon all people, in that all people sinned,
for until the coming of the law sin was in the world, and that sin was counted as nothing, because there was not yet a law.
But death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the times to come.

But the grace is not like the trespass. If through the trespass of that one man many perished, how much more have the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abounded to many!
And the gift is not as it was through that one who trespassed, for the judgment from that one led to condemnation, but the grace, from many trespasses, leads to justification.

If through the trespass of that one man death reigned through that one, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one Jesus Christ!
Just as from that one trespass it came upon all people for condemnation, so also through the righteousness of that one it came upon all people for justification of life.
Just as through the disobedience of that one man many entered as sinners, so also through the obedience of that one man many entered as righteous.
For the law came in between, so that sin might multiply, and where sin multiplied, there grace abounded all the more,
so that, as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign in righteousness to eternal life through Christ Jesus our Lord.
Now what shall we say? Shall we remain in sin so that grace may multiply? May it not be!
We who died to sin, how then shall we go on living in it?
Or do you not know that those of us who were baptized into Christ were baptized into his death?
And we were buried together with him by that baptism into his death, so that, as Christ rose from the dead by the glory of the Father, so also we might walk in renewal of life.
If we have become planted together with him in the likeness of his death, so also shall we be in his resurrection.
And know this, that our old man was crucified with him, so that the body of sin might be done away with and so that we might no longer serve sin,
for he who has died has been justified from sin.
If we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him.
This we know, that Christ rose from the dead and will die no more, and death will no longer have dominion over him.
For he who died, died to sin once, but he who lives, lives to God.
So also you, count yourselves dead to sin and alive to God through Christ Jesus.
Therefore let sin not reign over those mortal bodies of yours, so that you obey it in its desires,
nor present those members of yours to sin as instruments of falsehood, but present yourselves to God as living from the dead, and those members of yours to God as instruments of righteousness.
Sin shall not have dominion over you, for you are not under law, but under grace.
Now then, shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? May it not be!
Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as slaves in obedience, you are slaves of the one you obey, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
Thanks be to God, for you were slaves of sin, and you became obedient from the heart to the form of teaching to which you were handed over.
But now you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of righteousness.

I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh: just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness, unto lawlessness, so now present those members of yours as slaves to righteousness, unto holiness.
When you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.
What fruit, then, did you have at that time, from the things of which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.
But now you have been set free from sin and enslaved to God; you have your fruit unto righteousness, and as the end, eternal life.
For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Christ Jesus our Lord.
Or do you not know, brothers (for I speak to you as to those who know the law), that the law has authority over people for as long as a person is alive?
A married woman is bound by the law; if the husband dies, she is free from that law of the husband.

During the husband's lifetime it will be counted as adultery for her if she joins herself to another husband; but if the husband dies, she is free from that law, and it will not be counted as fornication for her if she joins herself to another husband.
Therefore, my brothers, you too have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, the one who was raised from the dead, in order that you may bear fruit for God.
For while we were in the flesh, the passions of sin that came through the law were at work in our members, so that we bore fruit for death.
But now we have been set free from the law and have died to that by which we were held captive, so that we may serve in renewed spirit and not in the aged letter.
What then shall we say? Is the law sin? May it not be! But I would not have known sin except through the law. For I would not have known desire if the law had not said: You shall not covet.
So sin found occasion through the commandment and produced in me every desire, for without the law sin was dead.
I was once alive without the law, and when the commandment came, sin came to life,
and I died; and that commandment [?], which was meant for life, itself became death for me.
For sin found occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
Therefore the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.

Did that which is good, then, become death for me? May it not be! Rather it was sin, so that it might appear as sin through the good thing that became death for me, so that sin might become exceedingly sinful through the commandment.
We know this, that the law is spiritual, and I am fleshly and raised in sin.
For what I do, I do not know; for I do not do what I want, but what I hate, that I do.
If I do what I do not want, I bear witness together with the law that it is good.
So now it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that has settled in me.
Know this: that good does not dwell with me, that is, in my flesh; for the will is present with me, but I have no power to do the good.
For I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I do not want, that I do.
If I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that dwells with me.
Do I then find a law, that when I want to do good, evil is present with me?
I am pleased with the law of God in my inner man.
And I see another law in my members, which are arrayed against the law of my mind and take me captive by the law of sin that is in my members.
Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this flesh of death?
But thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Is there then no condemnation for those who are of Christ Jesus?
For the law of the Spirit of life through Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death.
For what was impossible for the law, which was weak because of the flesh, God did: he sent his own Son in the likeness of the flesh of sin and on account of sin, and he condemned sin by that flesh,
so that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled among us, who conduct ourselves not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
For those who are according to the flesh think the things of the flesh, but those who are according to the Spirit think the things of the Spirit.
For the thinking of the flesh is death, but the thinking of the Spirit is life and peace.
For the thinking of the flesh is enmity toward God, for it does not submit to the law of God, nor can it.
For those who are in the things of the flesh cannot please God.
But you are not in the things of the flesh but of the Spirit, if the Spirit of God dwells among you. If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.
If Christ is among you, let the flesh be dead because of sin, but the spirit alive for righteousness.
If the Spirit that raised Jesus from the dead dwells among you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to these mortal bodies of yours, because of his Spirit that dwells among you.
So now, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, that we should live according to the flesh.
If you live according to the flesh, you are bound for death; if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the flesh, you will live.
For those who walk by the Spirit of God, they are the children of God.
For you have not received the spirit of slavery, so as to be afraid again, but you have received the spirit of adoption, by which we cry out: Abba, Father!
That same Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God.
If children, then also heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ.
For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy of the glory to come, which is to be revealed to us.
For the expectation of creation awaits the revealing of the sons of God,
for creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but by the one who subjected it, in hope,
for creation itself will also be set free from the oppression of corruption into the freedom and glory of the children of God.
This we know: that all creation groans together and suffers pain together until now.
And not only it, but we ourselves also, who have the firstfruit of the Spirit, groan within ourselves and await the adoption, the redemption of our bodies,
for we are saved by hope. But hope that is seen is not hope: for what someone sees, why would he still hope for it?
If we do not see and yet hope, we wait with patience.
Likewise the Spirit also helps our weakness, for we do not know what we should pray for as is fitting; but the Spirit itself intercedes for us with wordless sighing.
And he who searches the heart knows the thought of the Spirit, for it intercedes before God for the saints.
This you know: for those who love God, all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his decree.
For those whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers;
and those whom he predestined, he also called; and those whom he called, he also justified; and those whom he justified, he also glorified.
What then shall we say to this? If God is on our side, who is there to speak evil against us?
He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all, how will he not with him also grant us all things?
Who is an accuser of the chosen of God? God is the one who justifies.
And who is the one who condemns? Jesus Christ, who died, and more than that, rose; who sits at the right hand of God and intercedes for us.
Who will separate us from the love of Christ: tribulation or distress, persecution or hunger, nakedness or anguish or the sword? As it is written:
For your sake we are put to death every day, and we are counted as sheep for slaughter.
But in all this we will prevail through him who loved us.
I believe that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor archangels, nor this world, nor that world,
nor heights, nor depths, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is through Christ Jesus our Lord.
I speak the truth through Christ and do not lie, my mind bearing witness with me by the Holy Spirit,
for I have great sorrow and unceasing [?] pain of my heart.
I pray that I myself might be made accursed from Christ for the sake of my brothers and my kin according to the flesh,
who are Israelites, to whom belonged the adoption and the glory and the covenants and the givings of the law and the services of worship and the good tidings;
to whom belonged the fathers, from whom came Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever and ever. Amen.
It is not as though the word of God had fallen to the ground, for not all who are from Israel are Israel,
nor are all the descendants of Abraham his children; rather, "Through Isaac shall your seed be named."
That is, it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise who are reckoned as descendants.
For this is the word of the promise: "At this very time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son."
And not only so, but Rebekah also had children from one bed, by Isaac our father;
for they had not yet been born, nor had they done good or evil, so that God's purpose by election might stand,
not from works but from him who called. For it was said to her: "The elder shall serve the younger."
As it is written: "Jacob I loved, and Esau I hated."
What then shall we say? Is there falsehood with God? May it not be!
For he says to Moses: "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will show favor to whom I show favor."
So then it does not depend on the one who wills or on the one who runs, but on the one to whom God shows mercy.
For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: "For this very reason I raised you up, that I might show my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed over all the earth."
So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.
You will say to me then: "Why does he still blame me? Who has withstood his will?"
Now who are you, O man, to answer back to God? Will the thing made say to its maker: "Why did you make me like this?"
Or does the potter not have the power to make from the same kneaded clay some vessels for honor and some without honor?
What if God, wishing to show his wrath and make known his power, has endured with much long-suffering the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,
and did so in order to show the riches of his glory upon the vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,
even us, whom he also called, not only from among the Jews but also from among the Gentiles?
As he says to Hosea: "I called those not my people my people, and her who was not beloved, beloved."
"And it shall be that in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' there they shall be called children of the living God."
But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the sons of Israel be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall be saved;
for it is a word that accomplishes and cuts short in righteousness, for the Lord will carry out a shortened word upon the earth."
And as Isaiah foretold: "Had not the Lord Almighty left us descendants, we would have become like the Sodomites and been made like the Gomorrahites."
What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who were not seeking righteousness, have attained righteousness, the righteousness that comes from faith.
Israel pursued the law of righteousness and did not attain the law of righteousness.
Why so? Because they pursued it not from faith but as if from the works of the law, for they stumbled on that stone of stumbling.
As it is written: Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and everyone who believes in him will never be put to shame.
Brothers, the desire of my heart and my prayer to God for them is for their salvation.
And I bear them witness that they have zeal for God, but not with knowledge.
For they were ignorant of the righteousness of God and sought to establish their own, and they did not submit to the righteousness of God,
for the end of the law is Christ, as Savior of everyone who believes.
For Moses wrote thus: The righteousness that is from the law, the person who does it will live by it.
But concerning the righteousness that is from faith he says thus: Do not say in your heart, Who will go up to heaven? That is, to bring Christ down.
Or: Who will go down into the abyss? That is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
But what does it say? The word is near to your mouth and to your heart, that is, the word of faith that we preach,
that if you confess the Lord Jesus with your mouth and believe with your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
For with the heart you believe unto righteousness, and with the mouth you confess unto salvation.
For the book says: Everyone who believes in him will never be put to shame.
For there is no distinction between Jew and Gentile, for he himself is Lord of all, who makes rich all who call upon him.
Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.
How then will they call upon one in whom they have not believed? How then will they believe one whom they have not heard? Or how will they hear without preaching?
Or how will they preach unless someone sends them? As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the good news of peace, who bring good news of good things!
But not all have listened to the gospel. Isaiah says: Lord, who has believed what we have heard?
So then, faith comes from hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
But I say again: Have they not heard? For their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
But I say: Did Israel not understand? First Moses says: I will make them jealous over what is no nation, and with a senseless nation I will make them angry.
Isaiah dares to say: I was found by those who did not seek me, and I was revealed to those who did not ask for me.
But concerning Israel he says thus: All day long I have stretched out my hands toward a disobedient and contentious people.
But I say: Has God cast off his people? May it not be! For I too am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not rejected his people, whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says of Elijah, how he appeals to God in accusation against Israel:
"Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars; I alone am left, and they seek my life as well."
But what does the command of the word say to him? "I have left for myself as many as seven thousand men, whose knees have not bent to Baal."
So too at this present time a remnant has come to be by election, through grace.
If by grace, then no longer from works; if it were so, grace would not be counted as grace.
Now then, why does Israel seek this which it has not attained? But the elect attained it, and the others were blinded,
as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of sorrow, eyes so that they should not see and ears so that they should not hear, up to this very day."
And again David says: "Let their table become a snare before them, a recompense and a stumbling block.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see, and bend their backs continually!"
But this I say: have they then stumbled so that they should fall? Far from it! Rather, their transgression has become salvation for the Gentiles, in order to make them jealous.
If their transgression has become the riches of the world, and their stumbling the riches of the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness be!
But I say to you, you Gentiles: inasmuch as I am an apostle of the Gentiles, I will glorify this ministry of mine,
if only I may make my own flesh jealous and save some of them.
If their falling away has become the reconciliation of the world, how much more their acceptance, if not life from the dead?
If the beginning is holy, so also is what follows; and if the root is holy, so also are its branches.
If some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in upon them and became a sharer in the root and in the richness of the olive tree,
do not boast over those branches. If you do boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root that bears you.
But you will surely say: "The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in."
Very well! They were broken off through their unbelief, and you stand through faith. Do not be haughty, but be afraid!
If God did not spare those natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either.
Now then, see the kindness and the severity of God: severity upon those who fell, but kindness upon you, if you remain in that kindness; if not, you too will be cut off.
And they, if they do not remain in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
If you were cut off from what is by nature a wild olive and, contrary to nature, were grafted onto the good olive, how much more will these natural branches be grafted onto their own olive tree!

I do not wish you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own estimation: that blindness has come upon Israel for a time, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in.
And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion and will turn Jacob away from ungodliness."
And this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.
As regards the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but as regards election, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
For the graces and the callings of God are not repented of.
Just as you too were once disobedient to God, and have now received mercy through their disobedience,
so too these have now become disobedient for the sake of your being received, so that they too may be received.
For God has shut up all people in disobedience, so that he may have mercy on all.
O the depth and the riches and the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable are his ways!
Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?
Or who has first given anything to him, and been repaid by him?
For from him and through him and to him are all things. And his is the glory forever and ever. Amen.
I beseech you, brothers, by the mercy of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, which is your rational service.
And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may discern what the will of God is: good, pleasing and perfect.

For by the grace that has been given to me I say to everyone who is among you: do not think more highly of yourself than is proper, but think with purity of mind, each one as God has apportioned by the measure of faith.
For just as one body has many members, yet all the members do not have the same function,
so too we all are one body through Christ, and individually we are members of one another.
For we have the gift in various forms by the grace of God: whether prophecy, in keeping with the measure of faith,
or whoever serves, in that service;
or whoever comforts, in that comforting; whoever gives, with generosity; whoever presides, with diligence; whoever shows mercy, with cheerfulness,
with love without hypocrisy, shun evil and cling to what is good;
in brotherly love be affectionately loving toward one another; in showing honor outdo one another;
do not be lazy in zeal. Be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord;
rejoice in hope, endure in tribulation, be watchful in prayer;
share in the remembrance of the saints, pursue hospitality;
bless your persecutors, bless and do not curse;
rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep;
And be of the same mind toward one another; do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the lowly.
Do not be wise in your own eyes.
And let none of you repay evil for evil; take thought beforehand for what is good before God and before people.
If it is possible on your part, keep peace with all people.
Do not seek vengeance by yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath, as it is written: Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord.
But if your enemy is hungry, give him bread; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let every person submit to the higher authority, for there is no authority except from God; and those that are appointed are likewise from God.
Therefore whoever opposes that authority opposes God's command. And those who oppose it will bring judgment upon themselves.
For rulers are not a terror to those who do good, but to those who do evil. Do you want not to fear the authority? Do good, and you will receive praise from it,
for it is God's servant to you for good. If you do evil, be afraid, for it does not bear the sword in vain; for it is God's servant, an avenger in wrath upon the evildoer.
Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath, but also for the sake of conscience.
Therefore also pay tribute, for they are servants of God, devoted to this very labor.
Render to all what is owed: tribute to whom tribute is due, toll to whom toll is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due.
Owe nothing to anyone except love for one another. For whoever loves his neighbor has fulfilled the Law, which is this:

You shall not commit adultery, you shall not kill, you shall not steal, you shall not covet; and whatever other commandment there is, it is fulfilled in this one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
Love does no evil to a neighbor; love is the fulfiller of the Law.
And know this, that it is already the time for us to awaken from sleep. For salvation is now nearer to us than when we first believed.
The night has gone far from us, and the light has drawn near to us; now therefore let us put far from us the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
And as in the daytime, let us conduct ourselves becomingly, not in revelry and drunkenness, nor in beds of defilement, not in strife and envy,
but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make the will of the flesh into lust.
And receive the one who is weak in faith, not with doubt and with disputing thoughts.
One person believes he may eat everything, but the weak one eats herbs.
Let the one who eats not despise the one who does not eat; and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God has accepted them.
Who are you, that you judge another's servant? It is before his own master that he stands or falls; and stand he will, for the Lord is able to make him firm.
One person keeps the fast on selected days, another keeps the fast on all days; let each be fully assured in his own mind.

Whoever regards the day regards it for the Lord; and whoever does not regard the day, for the Lord likewise does not regard it; and whoever eats, eats for the Lord, and gives thanks to God; and whoever does not eat, for the Lord likewise does not eat, and gives thanks to God.
For none of us lives by himself, and none dies by himself.
If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, it is by the Lord too that we die; whether we are alive or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
For this is why Christ died and rose again: that he might be Lord over the dead and the living.
Now why do you judge your brother? Or why do you despise that brother of yours? For we are all to stand before the judgment seats of Christ.
As it is written: "I live, says the Lord, for to me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall confess to God."
So then, each one of us shall give an account of himself to God.
Let us no longer judge one another, but rather consider this instead: that you not put an obstacle or a stumbling block in a brother's way.
I know and am convinced by the Lord Jesus Christ that nothing is defiled in itself; but if anyone reckons something to be defiled, to him it is defiled.
If your brother is grieved on account of food, you are no longer walking in love. Do not by your food destroy him for whom Christ died.
And let that good of yours not be reviled.
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Whoever serves Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.
So then, pursue peace and the building up of one another.
Do not undo the work of God for the sake of food. All things are pure, but it is evil for the person who eats in doubt.
It is better not to eat meat, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything by which your brother stumbles or is tripped up.
Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself by that with which he tests his neighbor.
But whoever is of two minds, even if he eats, is condemned, for he does not eat in faith; and everything that is not of faith is sin.
Now to him who is able to establish you according to my gospel and the preaching of Christ Jesus, by the revelation of the mystery that was kept silent through eternal ages,
which has now been made manifest through the prophetic scriptures, by the command of the eternal God, made known to all the Gentiles for the obedience of faith,
to the only wise God, through Christ Jesus, whose is the glory forever and ever. Amen.
We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the feeble, and not merely to please ourselves,
but let each one of us also please his neighbor, for his good, for building up.
For Christ too did not please himself, but, as it is written: The reproaches of those who reproached you fell on me.
For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through the patience and the consolation of the scriptures we may have hope.
And may the God of patience and consolation grant you to be of the same mind toward one another in accordance with Christ Jesus,
so that together, with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore receive one another, just as Christ received you, to the glory of God.
for I say that Christ became a servant of the circumcision for the sake of God's truth, so that the promise made to the fathers might be firm,
and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy, as it is written: "Therefore I will confess you among the Gentiles and sing to your name."
And again he says: Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people.
And again he says: Praise the Lord, all you tribes, and sing to him, all peoples.
And again Isaiah says: And there shall be the root of Jesse, he who is to arise as ruler of the Gentiles, and in him the Gentiles shall hope.
Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope and in the power of the Holy Spirit.
I too am convinced concerning you, brothers, that you also are full of goodness and complete in all knowledge, and able also to teach one another.
Yet I have written to you rather boldly, brothers, in part as if reminding you, by the grace of God that has been given to me by God,
so that I may be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, laboring as a priest in the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable and holy by the Holy Spirit.
I have a boast through Christ Jesus before God.
For I will not dare to speak of anything that Christ has not done through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed,
and by the power of signs and wonders and by the power of the Holy Spirit; for from Jerusalem and round about as far as Illyricum I have been sent to fulfill the gospel of Christ.
Thus I was honored to preach the gospel, not where Christ has been named, so that I might not build upon another's foundation,
but as it is written: Those to whom nothing has been told about him shall see, and those who have not seen shall understand.
For this reason also I was greatly pressing forward [?] to come to you.
But now I no longer have any place in these regions here, and I have longed to come to you for many years.
When I go to Spain, I hope, when I am going there, also to see you, and to be sent on there by you, if I may first be satisfied in some measure by seeing you.
Now behold, I am going to Jerusalem to serve the saints.
For Macedonia and Achaia have seen fit to make some contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem.
They have seen fit, and they are also their debtors. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they ought also to serve them in bodily things.
When I have completed this and sealed their fruit, I shall go on by way of you to Spain,
and this I know, that when I come to you, I shall come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
I entreat you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to become fellow laborers with me in prayer to God on my behalf,
that I may be delivered from the disobedient in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
so that with the joy of the gospel I may come to you by the will of God and find rest with you.
And may the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the church of the people of Cenchreae,
that you may receive her in the Lord, as is worthy of the saints, and stand by her in whatever matter she may need; for she too has been a helper to many, and to me myself as well.
Greet Priscilla and Aquila, my fellow helpers in Christ Jesus,
who stretched out their necks for my life, to whom not only I am grateful, but all the churches of the Gentiles,
and greet the congregation in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.
Greet Mary, who has labored greatly for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsfolk and my fellow captives, who are renowned among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in Christ.
Greet Urbanus, my fellow helper in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.
Greet Apelles, chosen in Christ. Greet those of the household of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, who have labored in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who has labored greatly in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. The churches of Christ greet you.
I beseech you, brothers, beware of those who cause division and stumbling outside the teaching that you have learned, and keep far away from them.
For such people do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly, and by sweet talk and blessing they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
But may your obedience be renowned to all; I rejoice over you, and I want you to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil.
And the God of peace will crush the devil under your feet soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
Timothy, my helper, greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my fellow helpers.
I, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.
Gaius, host to me and to all the churches, greets you. Erastus, the steward of the city, greets you, and Quartus, our brother.
Now to him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, by the revelation of the mystery kept silent through the times of the ages,
which has now been made manifest through the prophetic writings, by the command of the eternal God, for the obedience of faith, revealed to all the Gentiles,
to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
